newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Late profit-taking erodes Taiwan stock gains.
newsitem.headline: Late profit-taking erodes Taiwan stock gains.

text.p: Profit-taking emerged in Taiwan's stock market after the index -- fuelled by Wall Street's record surge -- rose to hit resistance at 9,400 points, eroding Wednesday's early-session gains in late trade, brokers said.
Taiwan's index surged as high as 9,415.58 points, a yet another seven-year intraday high. With 50 minutes left, at 0310 GMT, the index was up 38.03 points or 0.41 percent at 9,343.30.
"Wall Street's performance recently has had a stronger impact on Taiwan stocks than it has in the past," said indepedent analyst Michael Hung.

"That's because Taiwan is following the U.S. pattern of upgrading its industry. Just as the U.S. is reengineering its high-technology industry to compete with Japan and Europe, Taiwan's high-tech electronic industry has seen the benefits of upgrading," Hung said.
Electronics led Wednesday's gains, rising 2.56 percent.

Microchip maker United Microelectronics was up T$6.5 to T$134.5 on its announcement of an afternoon news conference amid intense speculation that it had hired Donald Brooks, who until april was president of rival Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp.
Brokers said the index likely would rise further and soon test resistance at 9,500-9,600.
